predictions.selection_reason: property value check -> null/undefined comparison -> may allow prototype pollution if val is null/undefined and value is attacker-controlled object
predictions.source_summary: The 'value' parameter comes from iterating over properties of user-provided objects using forOwn, which includes inherited properties. The 'key' parameter is the property name from the source objects.
predictions.sink_summary: Direct assignment to o[key] = value when val is null/undefined, allowing property injection into the target object 'o'
predictions.guard_summary: No validation of property names (keys) before assignment. The isObject check only applies to nested objects, not to property name validation.
predictions.risk_pattern: Property assignment without key validation allows prototype pollution if attacker-controlled keys like '__proto__' or 'constructor' are used, potentially modifying Object.prototype
called_function_context: forOwn (iterates over object properties including inherited)
isObject (checks if value is plain object)
enclosing_conditions: else if (isObject(val) && isObject(value)) - triggers recursive merge
predictions.context_summary: The defaults function recursively merges properties from source objects into a target object, assigning values when target properties are null/undefined
unresolved_facts: Whether for-own library properly filters prototype properties
Whether is-plain-object library correctly identifies plain objects vs built-in prototypes
How this function is used in real applications and what data flows through it
